result.summary: Flipped REQ-202's status: pending -> done in docs/requirements.yaml. Appended one `done` event to docs/status/requirement_status.v7.yaml (the current volume per the index) summarizing the store, the deliberate canonicaliser/PromotionDigest separation, per-tenant placement, DB-level immutability, the REQ-041 disambiguation, and all five rework cycles (two real Postgres bugs TEST-DESIGNER's own test execution caught: an index-name collision plus a truncated-constraint-name mismatch, both from Ecto's default naming; one TEST-DESIGNER coverage gap; one oracle-rot test-fixture gap). Verified append-only via `git diff --numstat` (59 insertions, 0 deletions). Recounted volume 7's on-disk entries with `grep -c "^  - req:" docs/status/requirement_status.v7.yaml` = 22 (up from the declared 21, a clean +1, no concurrent sibling append found on this volume at write time) and updated the index's declared `entries:` to 22 in the same commit; volume is 733 lines / 43448 bytes, well under the 1200-line/120000-byte roll ceiling, so no roll triggered. Updated docs/migration/stage-6-operational-cross-cutting.md's running status paragraph to record REQ-202 done, matching the REQ-195/196 precedent, and noting REQ-203 (activation) as the pair's deferred other half. Filed two docs/anti-patterns.md entries: (1) a NEW entry on Ecto's default index/constraint naming silently colliding or exceeding Postgres's 63-byte NAMEDATALEN limit, invisible to a plain `mix ecto.migrate` because that never replays a migration into a fresh per-tenant schema; (2) a NEW entry (this bug class had never actually been filed here despite two prior handoffs claiming it was 'documented') covering the tenant_fixture.ex oracle-rot gap across all three real occurrences -- REQ-181, REQ-195, REQ-202 -- since no prior anti-patterns.md entry existed for either sibling session to have grepped for before REQ-202 hit it a third time.
